A decay chain $A \to B \to \emptyset$ from equations to a fit. Code generation needs a C++17
compiler and Python with SymPy ([Installation](installation.html)); models compile into
`tempdir()`, the default `outdir`.

```{r library}
library(cppDE)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Model definition and solution

`cppODE()` generates and compiles the solver of the equations. `solveODE()` returns the states and
their sensitivities, the derivatives in every initial value and parameter.

```{r chain}
eqns  <- c(A = "-k1*A", B = "k1*A - k2*B")
parms <- c(A = 1, B = 0, k1 = 0.5, k2 = 0.2)
times <- seq(0, 10, by = 0.1)

chain <- cppODE(eqns, modelname = "chain")
out   <- solveODE(chain, times, parms)

dim(out$tangent)                       # [time, state, parameter]
out$tangent[101, "B", ]                # ∂B(10) / ∂(A, B, k1, k2)
```

`longFormat()` ([listing](#helper-for-the-figures)) arranges states and sensitivities for the
figure.

```{r chain-plot, fig.height = 4.2}
ggplot(longFormat(out), aes(time, value)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y", ncol = 5) +
  scale_x_continuous(n.breaks = 3)
```

## Parameter estimation

The sensitivities give the gradient of a least-squares objective, here for $k_1$ and $k_2$ from
noisy readings of $B$. The output includes $t = 0$ (`includeTimeZero = TRUE`), so the data grid
starts there.

```{r fit}
set.seed(1)
tdata <- c(0, 1:10)
data  <- out$variable[match(tdata, times), "B"] + rnorm(length(tdata), sd = 0.01)

objective <- function(k) {
  sol <- solveODE(chain, tdata, c(A = 1, B = 0, k))
  res <- sol$variable[, "B"] - data
  structure(sum(res^2), gradient = 2 * colSums(res * sol$tangent[, "B", names(k)]))
}
fit <- optim(c(k1 = 1, k2 = 0.1), function(k) objective(k),
             function(k) attr(objective(k), "gradient"), method = "BFGS")
fit$par
```

The [Guide](guide-model.html) treats events, second-order and reverse-mode derivatives, steady
states, batches of conditions, algebraic functions and the SUNDIALS backend;
[dMod2](https://dmodverse.github.io/dMod2/) builds observation functions, parameter
transformations, objective functions, optimizers and profile likelihoods on cppDE.
